The employment rate was higher in Ontario than in Quebec in September 2026.

| Province | Employment rate, September 2026 | Vector |
|---|---|---|
| Ontario | 60.1% | v2063951 |
| Quebec | 59.9% | v2063762 |

Ontario was ahead by 0.2 percentage points. That gap is small, and these are survey estimates, so it may not be statistically significant.

These figures are seasonally adjusted rates for the population aged 15 and over, both genders combined. The source is Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey, table 14-10-0287-01, released 2026-10-09.

Canada's youth unemployment rate (ages 15 to 24) was **13.0% in September 2026**, down from **14.6% in September 2025**. That is a drop of 1.6 percentage points over the year.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Labour Force Survey, table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2062842. The series is Canada, both genders, ages 15 to 24, unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted.
- **Reference periods:** September 2026 (released 2026-10-09) and September 2025.
- **Revised figure:** The 2025 value is the revised figure now in the table. It may differ from what was first published, because seasonally adjusted data are revised each year.

Canada lost about 68,300 jobs in September 2026, according to the Labour Force Survey (LFS).

- Employment was 21,104.8 thousand in September, down from 21,173.1 thousand in August. That is a drop of 68.3 thousand, or about 0.3%.
- The figures are seasonally adjusted and cover everyone aged 15 and over.
- The monthly change is my own subtraction of the two published levels. I did not look up Statistics Canada's own stated change.
- I did not check the coordinate's dimension labels in the table metadata. I'm relying on the vector ID for the identification.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2062811 (Employment, Canada, both sexes, 15 years and over, seasonally adjusted). The reference period is September 2026, released 2026-10-09.

The average hourly wage of employees in Canada was **$37.64** in September 2026. That is **$0.86 (about 2.3%) higher** than the $36.78 in September 2025.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0063-01 (Labour Force Survey), vector v2132579.
- **Series:** Average hourly wage rate, Canada, all employees (full- and part-time), all industries, both genders, ages 15 and over. The figures are unadjusted for seasonality.
- **Reference periods:** September 2026, released 2026-10-09, and September 2025.
- **Calculation:** The percentage change is my own calculation from the two published values. I did not look up a published year-over-year figure.

In August 2026, Canada's job vacancy rate was **2.8%**, with about **507,220 vacant positions**. Both figures are seasonally adjusted and cover all industries.

- The vacancy rate was also 2.8% in June and July 2026.
- Vacancies were about 502,030 in July, so August is up by roughly 5,200 positions.
- Statistics Canada released the data on 2026-10-29. The status code on each value is 3, which I did not look up.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0406-01 (Job vacancies, payroll employees, and job vacancy rate by industry sector, monthly, seasonally adjusted).
- Vacancies: vector v1446283287
- Vacancy rate: vector v1446283289

Canada's all-items CPI rose **3.1%** in the 12 months to September 2026.

- The index was 170.0 in September 2026 and 164.9 in September 2025 (2002=100).
- The change is 170.0 ÷ 164.9 − 1 = 3.09%, which rounds to 3.1%. I calculated this from the index levels. I did not read it from a published year-over-year series.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01 (Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted), Canada, all-items, vector v41690973. Reference period: September 2026 against September 2025. The September 2026 figure was released on 2026-10-19.

Gasoline prices in Canada were **27.8% higher** in September 2026 than in September 2025.

- The gasoline CPI index (2002=100) rose from 209.4 in September 2025 to 267.6 in September 2026. I calculated the percentage from those two index values.
- Prices also rose from the previous month. The index was 252.2 in August 2026, so September was about 6.1% higher.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01 (Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted), Canada, Gasoline, vector v41691136. Reference periods: September 2025 and September 2026.
